states.instruction: Write down the material state, whether either king is in check, and the immediate threats available to both sides.
If our king is in check, answer it. If they have mate in one, mate now or play a forcing move that removes every mate in one.
Try our moves in the configured threat order. Finish one threat class before entering the quiet rules.
The defender tries mate, checks, direct answers to our threat, and counterattacks that meet or beat our payoff. Explore those replies in that order.
After every enabled first-order threat has been tried and stopped, use a position rule such as attacking the defender of a loose piece.
If an otherwise strong root line fails only because of one forcing reply, try one root move that makes that reply illegal and still creates a named threat.

stop_their_mate_in_one.when: only when the defending side has mate in one

check.when: unless our king is already mated; while in check, keep only legal check answers

threaten_mate_in_one.when: when mate now is unavailable and the configured ply limit has not been reached

take_material.when: when the capture reaches the material objective after the defender's immediate recaptures

double_attack.when: when the smaller target is valuable enough to reach the material objective

threats.quietWhen: No enabled mate, check, mate-in-one threat, objective-winning capture, or objective-relevant double attack survives its defender test.

predicates.definition: The side to move has no legal answer to check.
A legal move gives check; record how many legal answers it allows and what else it attacks.
A legal move threatens mate on the next move.
If the other side could move now, it has a mating move.
The side to move is in check.
The fighting side is behind in material, so a material line must recover the deficit and still reach the objective.
The fighting side has not yet reached the configured material objective.
Every enabled first-order threat has been tried and stopped; position rules may now be tried.
A non-king is attacked and has no pawn defender.
A friendly piece attacks the occupied target square.
One piece defends two or more loose pieces.
A legal capture reaches the material objective after the defender's immediate recapture choices.
A legal move attacks the king and a valuable piece, or two valuable pieces, with enough payoff to reach the objective.
A legal move attacks a defender of one or more loose pieces; ignoring it loses enough material to meet the objective.
Capture a loose piece; an immediate recapture permits a double attack.
A defender reply mates, checks, creates mate in one, or counterattacks for at least the value of the active threat.

rules.instruction: Answer the check and prefer the answer that creates the highest-ranked threat.
Name the loose piece and its defender. Try attacking the defender, then capture-recapture-double-attack ideas, then a direct capture.

outcomes.fightingSideWins: At least one fighting move reaches the objective against every ranked defender answer.
outcomes.defendingSideHolds: One ranked defender answer prevents the objective, or the configured perpetual cycle is reached.
outcomes.notEnoughInformation: The depth, move, position, or rule budget ends before either result is established.
